q: A student gives a wrong answer in class. The best first response is to:
a: Ask them to explain their thinking, then guide them to the right idea
w: Tell them the correct answer and move on
Ask another student to correct them
Ignore it so they are not embarrassed
e: Understanding the reasoning shows the misconception.

q: To check that the whole class has understood a concept, a teacher should:
a: Use a quick check such as mini whiteboards or a short exit question
w: Ask "Does everyone understand?"
Ask only the best student
Move on if nobody asks a doubt
e: Every student answers, so the teacher sees the whole class.

q: In a mixed-ability class, the best approach is to:
a: Offer tasks at different levels of challenge towards the same learning goal
w: Give the same task to everyone
Give extra homework only to weaker students
Teach at the level of the strongest students
e: Differentiation keeps every learner working towards the same goal.

q: A student keeps disturbing others. The teacher should first:
a: Speak to the student privately to understand the reason and agree expectations
w: Send the student out of the class
Shout to set an example
Report the student to the principal straight away
e: A private, respectful talk addresses the cause and keeps the relationship.

q: Which is the best learning objective for a lesson?
a: By the end, students will be able to label the parts of a plant cell
w: Students will learn about cells
The teacher will cover the cell chapter
Students will be interested in cells
e: A good objective says what students will be able to do, so it can be checked.

q: A student privately tells a teacher they are being harmed at home. The teacher should:
a: Listen kindly, not promise secrecy, and tell the school's safeguarding lead the same day
w: Keep it a secret to protect the student's trust
Confront the parents directly
Wait to see whether it happens again
e: Children's safety comes first, and concerns must go to the designated person.

q: A parent is upset about their child's marks. The best response is to:
a: Listen calmly, show the evidence and agree the next steps together
w: Defend the marks and end the meeting
Refuse to meet
Change the marks to keep the peace
e: Calm listening and evidence build trust.

q: Which feedback helps a student improve most?
a: Specific comments linked to the goal that say what to do next
w: Only a grade
Only praise
Only corrections in red ink
e: Students need to know what to do next.

q: A good way to start a new topic is to:
a: Begin with a real-life question or demonstration students can relate to
w: Read out the definitions
Start with a test on the topic
Give a long lecture first
e: A hook creates curiosity and connects to what students know.

q: A student finds reading difficult. The teacher should:
a: Provide support such as simpler text, extra time and one-to-one help, while keeping the student included
w: Seat the student at the back
Exclude the student from reading activities
Compare the student's reading with others in class
e: Support removes the barrier without lowering expectations.

q: After asking a question, a teacher should:
a: Wait a few seconds so more students can think before taking answers
w: Pick the first hand that goes up
Answer it themselves quickly
Only ask volunteers
e: Wait time improves the quality and number of answers.

q: When using technology in class, the teacher should:
a: Use it for a clear learning purpose, not just to fill time
w: Use it in every lesson regardless of purpose
Avoid it completely
Let students use it freely without guidance
e: Technology should serve the learning goal.
